brief: Standard Chartered has been bearish on the long end of the UST curve all year. The 10Y yield outran its forecast because the Fed's 16 September hike (25bps) was more hawkish than expected. SC raised its terminal Fed rate forecast by 50bps and expects another hike in December. Short end pricing already reflects about 50bps more tightening than SC or the median FOMC dots project, so until inflation confidence returns, rate hike pricing is likely to be pushed back rather than reduced, meaning the 2Y yield may not peak until after the December hike. The current curve flattening should hold through that hike, but SC expects long end yields to lead the curve steeper again in 2027, kept bearish by persistent AI related issuance, US fiscal concerns and Japanese repatriation risk, plus an inflation uncertainty risk premium even as oil's yield impact fades. SC raises its 2Y forecast to 4.8% (from 4.1%) for end-2026 and 4.6% (from 4.0%) for end-Q3-2027, and its 10Y forecast to 5.1% (from 4.6%) for end-2026, with scope to 5.5% within 12 months.
